title: Client FileBrowser implementation
body: This is an implementation of FileBrowser as it's described in the design doc. tl;dr of server/README.md and client/README.md to get this running: ```sh $ cd client $ make $ cd server $ make # (trust the .keys/ca-cert.pem certificate that was generated) $ yarn run start # (navigate to https://localhost:8443/filebrowser in a web browser) ``` Preview: Note: the git base of this PR is a temporary merge commit of `t/server/filebrowser` and `t/client/login`, both of which have outstanding PRs (#5 and #6). I'll rebase to `main` once those PRs are merged.

title: Server /api/filebrowser implementation
body:
- Added FILEBROWSER_ROOT environment variable to represent the root
  directory from which to list entries for /api/filebrowser
- Moved processing of environment variables into src/config.ts (now that
  more than one file needs to access them)

Note: this is using the `t/server/login` branch as a base because it depends on the session management implemented in that branch. I'll rebase to `main` once PR #4 is merged.

title: Client Login implementation
body:
This includes:

- Login form
- A basic Router
- A global store (src/store/index.ts). Used only for keeping track of
  the `sessionId` as of this commit.
- A wrapper for authenticated requests: `makeAuthenticatedRequest` (in
  src/store/actions.ts). This will be used to keep the store's
  `sessionId` in sync with the server when an authenticated request
  indicates an invalid or expired sessionId. Note: there are no
  authenticated requests yet; FileBrowser will have one
  (`/api/filebrowser`).
- A stub for the FileBrowser component. This is for Login to have
  something to forward to on successful login.

**Note:** this is using the `t/server/login` branch as a base because it depends on the `/api/login` endpoint. I'll rebase to `main` once PR #4 is merged.

title: server /api/login endpoint
body:
This PR implements the `/api/login` endpoint along with:

1. Session management
2. Unit tests and a test runner (because this is the first endpoint implementation). To run tests, use `yarn run tests`.
3. Authn/authz for the `/api/filebrowser` endpoint. This is still a stub on success. It's only meant to demonstrate auth-related failure codes.

A few nonautomated tests you can make against these endpoints are:

```
# run the server
$ yarn run start

# if you use HTTPie like I have in these examples, you'll need a concatenated certificate
$ cat .keys/ca-cert.pem .keys/server-cert.pem > bundle.pem

# a failed login
http --verify=bundle.pem POST https://localhost:8443/api/login username=zach password=hunter3

# login with a missing password param
http --verify=bundle.pem POST https://localhost:8443/api/login username=zach

# a successful login
http --verify=bundle.pem POST https://localhost:8443/api/login username=zach password=hunter2

# test a successfully-authenticated route
$ http --verify=bundle.pem https://localhost:8443/api/filebrowser 'Session-Id:SESSION_ID_FROM_ABOVE_RESPONSE'

# test an invalid session id
$ http --verify=bundle.pem https://localhost:8443/api/filebrowser 'Session-Id:dummy'
```

Users are currently hard-coded into `src/model/user.ts`. If you want to
generate your own, I've provided a script to compute the salt and passwordHash:

```
$ scripts/generate-user
Username: <input your username>
Password: <input your password>
# output:
{
  username: 'zach',
  salt: '7b2c4fb30a242346a359e90f94b043e8',
  passwordHash: 'e9045ae274855d15433b1d5058206ea9def9c4c07041bffd8805d61fc5ab0fa1',
  scopes: [ 'read:filebrowser' ]
}
```
